title: Probabilistic prioritizer: map RICE to token-economics & SLA regimes
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Goal: Design and pilot a 'Probabilistic Prioritizer' that extends classic RICE scoring to incorporate per-initiative token economics and latency/SLO regimes. This ticket scopes the PM workstream: framework spec, evaluation dataset, tooling hooks for cycle planning, and a small pilot across two initiatives (Console cost breakdown & Dedicated autoscaling). We want decisions to be auditable (how a score changes when token unit cost or SLO weight shifts) and easily mappable to OKRs and Initiative KPIs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Documented scoring algorithm that outputs: adjusted_score, confidence_band, sensitivity_to_unit_token_cost. 2) Example run for at least two initiatives with data inputs, showing ranking delta vs classic RICE. 3) A one-page PRD and Jupyter notebook demonstrating Monte Carlo sampling of reach/impact/effort/cost distributions. 4) A short demo in the roadmap review meeting and acceptance from Eng and Finance stakeholders.
metrics: expected token-cost delta (USD/month) for top-3 picks
probability(top-1 remains same) under +/-20% cost shock
plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): Research & spec. Gather historical initiative telemetry (effort estimates, realized impact, token usage profiles). Phase 2 (2 wks): Implement prototype — Monte Carlo RICE with cost-aware impact transforms; notebook and sample data. Phase 3 (1 wk): Pilot on 2 initiatives; collect feedback. Phase 4 (1 wk): Iterate and produce one-pager & demo. Deliverable: PRD, notebook, slide deck for roadmap review.
risks_and_tradeoffs: More complex scoring reduces transparency for non-technical stakeholders
Monte Carlo requires credible priors; garbage-in -> garbage-out
May overweight cost signals for infra-heavy initiatives vs long-term platform bets
Operationalizing distributional inputs requires coordination with Finance/Observability
